description: WIRE_FORMAT.md §23 — host-declared kind admission policy. Each case names a document, a declared policy, and the outcome a conformant decoder must produce. The point of the family is the PAIRING: the same bytes are admitted under one policy and refused under another, so what is pinned is that the narrowing is host-side and the default is unchanged. This manifest is HAND-AUTHORED and is not emitted by any host's corpus generator (the sanitization/ precedent); the root manifest.json is generated and would overwrite entries added here.

policies.description: The shipped default. Indistinguishable from declaring no policy at all — a host that supplies nothing MUST behave exactly as this.

The recommended profile for an application that uses no escape hatches: every kind in the root manifest's `kinds` vocabulary EXCEPT the two named here. Stated as an exclusion FROM THE VOCABULARY rather than as a literal admitted list, because restating forty kind names here would make this file a second source of truth for a vocabulary the root manifest already owns. A host resolves it to an allow-list at construction, so a kind added to the language later is not admitted by this profile.

cases.description: the control for `closed-refuses-custom` — the same bytes, decoding unchanged under the default
a root Custom node — the host-registered-renderer half of the guest boundary
a root Mount node — the guest-composition half of the guest boundary

the control for `closed-refuses-nested-custom`. This document is authored in THIS directory rather than referenced from nodes/, because the root corpus carries no fixture with a Custom below the root and the emitter would delete one added there.

a Custom node BELOW the root, inside an admitted Box. The whole tree is refused and the path names the offending node — a policy that only checked the root would admit this document and is the obvious wrong implementation
the closed profile is a NARROWING, not a refusal of everything: a tree using no hatch kind decodes under it exactly as under the default

a discriminator the VOCABULARY does not have, under a narrowing policy. It must still report WRONG_NODE_KIND: `no such kind` and `not admitted here` are different facts with different repairs, and a policy that swallowed the first would send an author to invent a spelling that is already correct
